name: isPhishingResistantOnlyEnabled
definition: The identity provider permits only phishing-resistant authenticators (FIDO2/WebAuthn, U2F, smart card or certificate-based authentication in multi-factor mode) for the whole organisation: at least one is enabled and no phishable method is.
population: Every authenticator or authentication method the organisation has enabled for its members, read from the tenant-wide catalogue (Okta GET /api/v1/org/factors; Entra authenticationMethodsPolicy). Guest-only methods are judged as Entra's implementation documents. Not administrators specifically -- that is isAdminMFAPhishingResistant.
evidenceRequiredForTrue: A COMPLETE, single-page read of the tenant's method catalogue showing at least one phishing-resistant method enabled and every enabled method phishing-resistant. A method enabled with no targets is not enabled for anyone (Entra, Tx #995). Okta FastPass alone never yields true: it is phishing-resistant only under an authentication-policy rule the catalogue cannot show.

openDecisions.question: May Okta - Application (f799acf0-d748-420b-8799-21fa7dde5f5d) answer this key? allowedIntegrations above records the rule as reported (Okta 3bc425fa only, not Okta - Application), which is also exactly today's wiring. The evidence below points the other way and has not been reconciled.
positions: As reported in the origin of the G1 ask: the key is valid only on the Okta definition (3bc425fa), not on Okta - Application (f799acf0). Encoded above; Integration-Service would reject an f799acf0 RTA row for this key.

QC F-iam-mfa-05 recommends the opposite: ADD the row to Okta - Application, method listOrgFactors, which is already in its workflow and succeeds today against a Spektrum-owned Okta org (spektrum-labs-cli reports/qc-2026-10-06/findings/iam-mfa.md, F-iam-mfa-05 and the listOrgFactors validation block).
The transform's own header names both: 'Vendor: Okta (also Okta - Application)' (safeguards/iam/okta/isPhishingResistantOnlyEnabled.py:3).

A third reading questions the SOURCE rather than the integration: on Okta Identity Engine, enforcement lives in authentication policies, and a factor ACTIVE in the org catalogue says nothing about whether a policy permits it ('same source, same doubt'; spektrum-labs-cli docs/okta-mfa-check-set-defects.md:47, :125-135). If that holds, neither Okta definition should answer from /api/v1/org/factors, and the fix is a policy read, not an allowlist.

implementations.meaning: Org factor catalogue: true when a phishing-resistant factor is ACTIVE and no phishable factor is; mixed reads false; FastPass-only, partial or paged reads are not measured.

notes: This is the key that started G1. The meaning is not contested: both vendors' implementations read a tenant-wide method catalogue and agree on type. What is contested is WHO may answer it, which is exactly what integrationPolicy: listed makes enforceable at Integration-Service's definition write path.
